beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Access is not absorption
beats.got: nothing new, a title

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Our licence count says nothing about whether anyone uses the tool. Fair, though I already suspected it.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: A real failure where good analysis got no decision because leaders trusted people, not the work. I've lived that, and it's a story about someone else's company but it's honest.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy easily, but the person who answers for the agent does not. So my team of fourteen needs a named owner.

beats.trigger: Share the output, and it has to appear where they already look, often enough to become a habit.
beats.got: Each of the four sharing forms asks something different of the receiver. Most of this repeats the exercise, but the output point suits my pricing brief.

beats.trigger: Not *how do I get them to adopt this?* but *what would have to be true for them to switch?*

beats.trigger: Have the conversation before you build anything more.

beats.trigger: It is rarely the same person across all four.
beats.got: Different teammates need different forms, so I'll map my fourteen against the four.

take_homes: Interview for the teammate's job first, then pick the sharing form (context, skill, output or interface) by the outcome. Infrastructure is not a reason.
You can copy context, boundary and checks, but the person who answers for the agent can't be copied. My shared context files have no named owner, and that is my team's real gap.
Ask what would have to be true for someone to switch, and test that with one person before building more.

monday.move: Talk to one pricing-working-group teammate about how they build the pilot-cohort brief today. Then test whether the brief appearing in their usual channel, as pushed output, would replace what they do.
monday.who: The analyst on my team who currently builds the cohort numbers by hand. I'd also name an owner for the shared context folder.
monday.when: Monday morning, 30 minutes, before I rerun the brief with fresh data.
monday.stop_condition: If they say they'd keep their own spreadsheet whatever the output looks like, I drop the push-output plan and rethink.
monday.blocker: We still have no shared place for context files, and nobody owns one.

misconception.why: I came thinking better prompts were the skill. This module says sharing fails on ownership and absorption, not prompt quality, which fits my team's private copies. I still think prompt quality matters, so shaken, not changed.

one_line: Useful if you're about to roll something out to a team, because it makes you name one person and one test. The lecture repeats the exercises, and the other-company story is honest but not mine.
